Method of Attack: The package includes a few strange binaries, including a single exe file, a single DLL file, and an encrypted dat file. The only JavaScript file present, index.js, simply executes a batch file that attempts to launch the executable file. After reversing the executable we ultimately uncovered the deployment of RAT through a relatively complicated process that convincingly masqueraded as a standard Microsoft update process.
Attack Vector: The package does not execute upon installation. Instead, it exports a function called compat which triggers the execution chain. The package description from the package.json claims that this package can be used to 'make project to be compatible with chromeOS', potentially fooling users into integrating this package into their project.
